messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Dutch, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Dutch line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Hij leek tegen mij aan te komen met het hoofd hoog en met een woedende honger, zodat het leek dat de lucht door hem trilde.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | Questi | demonstrative pronoun, “this one / he” | **Hij** | he | OK | | parea | “seemed” (imperfect) | **leek** | seemed | OK | | che (1) | complementizer introducing the motion clause | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | contra | preposition “against” | **tegen** | against | OK | | me | 1st‑person pronoun “me” | **mij** | me | OK | | venisse | subjunctive “to be coming” | **aan te komen** | to come | OK | | con (1) | preposition “with” (first attribute) | **met** | with | OK | | la | definite article “the” (feminine) | **het** | the | OK | | test' | noun “head” | **hoofd** | head | OK | | alta | adjective “high” | **hoog** | high | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **en** | and | OK | | con (2) | preposition “with” (second attribute) | **met** | with | OK | | rabbiosa | adjective “ravenous, ferocious” | **woedende** | raging / furious | **WRONG** (semantic mismatch) | | fame | noun “hunger” | **honger** | hunger | OK | | sì | resultative adverb “so that” | **zodat** | so that | OK | | che (2) | complementizer introducing result clause | **dat** | that | OK | | parea (2) | “seemed” (imperfect) | **leek** | seemed | OK | | che (3) | complementizer introducing inner clause | **dat** | that | OK | | l'aere | noun “the air” | **de lucht** | the air | OK | | ne | clitic pronoun “by him/it” (causal) | **door hem** | by him | OK | | tremesse | subjunctive “trembled” | **trilde** | trembled | OK |
### Issues Detected - **UNNECESSARY**: *che* (first) in line 46 is omitted in Dutch because the infinitival construction “aan te komen” does not require an explicit complementizer. - **WRONG**: *rabbiosa* rendered as **woedende** (“furious”) does not convey the intended sense of “ravenous” or “ferocious hunger”. A more accurate Dutch rendering would be **ravenende** or **hongerige**.
All other mappings are correct and grammatically appropriate.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Dutch script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Dutch text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
